taxonomyNote: Wikipedia notes some authorities treat it as a subspecies of Phasianus colchicus; Bishop Museum's Hawaii monograph files the Hawaii 'Green Pheasant' as Phasianus colchicus versicolor.
fieldMarks: Male: dark green breast, neck, mantle and flanks, bluish-purplish hood with ear tufts, red wattles, long pale grey-banded tail
Female: smaller than male, shorter tail, brownish-black with dark brown feathers fringed pale brown
behavior: Omnivorous: worms, insects, grains and plants
habitat: Woodland and forest edges, brush, grassland and parkland.
range: Native to Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu and smaller Japanese islands; introduced populations in Hawaii are reported stable; introduction to mainland North America was unsuccessful, and it has been crossed with common pheasants on some North American game farms.

lookalikes.name: Ring-necked pheasant
lookalikes.howToTell: Considered by some authorities the same species; Hawaii records also mention a melanistic 'mutant' or blue form of ring-necked pheasant that can resemble green pheasant.
